original_question: How many amino acids are present in the protein encoded by the gene associated with Type 2A Megalencephalic Leukoencephalopathy?

final_qi.question: How many amino acids are present in the protein encoded by the gene associated with Type 2A Megalencephalic Leukoencephalopathy?
final_qi.long_answer: Type 2A Megalencephalic Leukoencephalopathy (MLC2A) is caused by biallelic mutations in the GLIALCAM (also called HEPACAM) gene. GLIALCAM encodes the glial cell adhesion molecule, a single-pass type I membrane glycoprotein that is 416 amino acids in length in its canonical (isoform 1) sequence. Thus, the protein produced by the gene implicated in MLC2A contains 416 amino acids.

final_answer.long_answer: Type 2A Megalencephalic Leukoencephalopathy (MLC2A) is caused by recessive mutations in the HEPACAM (also called GlialCAM) gene. The canonical human HEPACAM protein sequence recorded in RefSeq (NP_079144.2) and UniProt (Q9P288) comprises exactly 416 amino acids. Thus, the protein encoded by the gene linked to MLC2A is 416 amino acids long.
